definitions.gloss: to ooze out; to seep through
definitions.explanation: To slowly leak or flow out through a surface, as liquid gradually penetrates or emerges.

definitions.gloss: to show through; to come to the surface
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, for emotions or inner qualities to gradually become visible or apparent.

examples.japanese: {傷口|きずぐち}から{血|ち}が{染|し}み{出|だ}してきた。
examples.english: Blood started to ooze from the wound.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}の{隙間|すきま}から{水|みず}が{少|すこ}しずつ{染|し}み{出|だ}している。
examples.english: Water is slowly seeping out through a crack in the wall.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れが{顔|かお}に{染|し}み{出|だ}す。
{彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}から{寂|さび}しさが{染|し}み{出|だ}していた。
examples.english: A sense of loneliness was coming through in his words.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{笑顔|えがお}には{優|やさ}しさが{染|し}み{出|だ}していて、{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}を{安心|あんしん}させた。
examples.english: Kindness showed through her smile, putting those around her at ease.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
{染|し}みる (to soak in, to permeate) + {出|だ}す (to start, to begin to come out)

TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive) - the liquid or quality comes out on its own

ASPECT ({ている}):
{染|し}み{出|だ}している indicates an ongoing state of seeping or oozing.

RELATED COMPOUND VERBS:
- {溢|あふ}れ{出|だ}す: to overflow
- {流|なが}れ{出|だ}す: to flow out
- {滲|にじ}み{出|だ}す: to ooze out (similar meaning)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {血|ち}が{染|し}み{出|だ}す: blood oozes out
- {水|みず}が{染|し}み{出|だ}す: water seeps out
- {油|あぶら}が{染|し}み{出|だ}す: oil seeps out
